## Experience

A reviewer opens the link and is solving a puzzle within 30 seconds, with no data or watch knowledge needed.

**Layout:** the movement on the left (escapement, balance, simplified gear train), the timegrapher trace and readouts on the right, controls below.

**Watch picker:** a dropdown of movements to work on. Each entry is a parameter set for the same simulation core: beat rate, balance inertia, mainspring torque curve, tooth count, and which puzzles apply. Start with one calibre; add a second (for example an 18,000 bph vintage movement and a 28,800 bph modern one) only once the core is stable, so the picker shows the physics changing rather than only the artwork.

**Controls:**

- Regulator index (shortens or lengthens the effective hairspring)
- Mainspring state of wind (full to run down)
- Balance inertia (timing screws)
- Beat adjustment
- Watch position (dial up, crown down, and so on)
- Time speed: real time to slow motion of one beat

**Demo mode = diagnosis puzzles.** Each puzzle loads a bundled faulty watch with a symptom and a goal:

| Puzzle | Symptom | Hidden cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runs fast | Gains about 40 s/day | Regulator off-centre | Move the index toward slow |
| Out of beat | Uneven tick, high beat error | Hairspring stud rotated | Adjust the beat |
| Afternoon slump | Fine when wound, drifts by evening | Low amplitude as the mainspring runs down | Explain the trade-off; there is no single knob |
| Position error | Good dial up, bad crown down | Poise error | Compare positions on the trace |

Puzzle 1 ships first; the others follow. Puzzle 3 is the teaching moment: some errors are physics, not adjustment.

**Difficulty ladder (stretch):** puzzles are ordered from one-knob fixes (Runs fast) to multi-cause faults (Position error) to open-ended builds. Later puzzles can require background reading: each links to the relevant section of Ciechanowski's *Mechanical Watch* as the "manual", so the Bench is the lab and the blog post is the textbook. The capstone is **Make your own complication**: given the gear train's output, the user wires up a date wheel or power-reserve indicator by choosing ratios and triggers, and the Bench checks that it advances correctly. This doubles as the complication stretch item in Scope.

## Scope

The core is one movement, one instrument and a handful of puzzles; stretch items are added only after the core is deployed and stable.

**Core:**

- Swiss lever escapement, balance wheel and hairspring, drawn to stay visually correct
- Mainspring torque curve feeding amplitude
- Timegrapher: tick trace, rate, amplitude, beat error
- Diagnosis puzzles, starting with one
- Watch picker with one calibre

**Stretch, in priority order:**

1. More puzzles and watch positions
2. A second calibre in the picker, with different physics
3. One complication, built as the capstone puzzle (a date wheel is the cheapest; a chronograph is a second gear train and is out)

**Out:**

- 3D rendering; automatic winding; multiple complications
- Any runtime LLM or backend
- Mobile-first layout (it must not break on a phone, but desktop is the target)

**Ordering rule for the agent:** core items are built and deployed before any stretch item starts. Stretch items go in the order above, each as its own branch, so an unfinished one never blocks the submission.

## Architecture

Simulation and rendering are strictly separate, so a bad drawing can never corrupt the physics and a renderer can be swapped without touching tested code.

&#91;embedded content: architecture · sim core, two views, tests\]

Controls and puzzles set parameters; the core advances state each tick; the movement view and timegrapher only read it. A watch catalog (one JSON entry per calibre) feeds the controls, so a new watch is data, not code. A complication would be a second state machine driven by the gear train's output. Stack: Vite + TypeScript + plain SVG, Vitest for the core, Playwright for render checks, static deploy.

## Escapement spike

The spike tests the riskiest visual — the escapement locking and releasing in sync with the balance — in a throwaway page, timeboxed to 45 minutes.

**Setup (5 min):** a fresh repo folder `spike/`, one HTML file plus one TypeScript module, Vite dev server, Playwright installed for screenshots. Keep the spike out of the main app; it may be thrown away.

**Steps:**

1. **Parameterized geometry (10 min).** Ask Claude to define the escape wheel (15 teeth), pallet fork and balance from a small set of named parameters: tooth count, lift angles, lock angle, drop. Shapes must be derived from those numbers, never hand-drawn paths.
2. **State machine before pictures (10 min).** Model one beat as phases: lock → unlock → impulse → drop → lock. Write tests first (`/tdd`): the escape wheel advances exactly half a tooth per beat; the pallet never overlaps a tooth; the balance swings both ways.
3. **Render (10 min).** Draw the state as flat SVG in a technical-drawing style. The renderer reads state only; it computes nothing.
4. **Look and correct (10 min).** Screenshot five phases of one beat with Playwright. Have Claude compare each frame to the phase it should show, and fix what is off.
5. **Slow-motion check.** Play one beat at 1/20 speed and watch it yourself. Your eye is the final judge.

**Prompt seed for step 1:**

Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page: - Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color. - Using all caps for labels. - Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits: 1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell); 2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; 3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns; 4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration; 5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles. - Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values. - Type: the typefaces and their roles. - Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified? - Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

/** SVG renderer. Reads state, computes nothing: every coordinate comes from shapes(). */
import { type EscapementParams } from "../core/escapement/params";
import { type EscapementPose } from "../core/escapement/kinematics";
import { shapes, stoneOutline, type Stone } from "../core/escapement/shapes";
import { type Polygon, type Vec, polar, add } from "../core/escapement/geom2d";

const pts = (poly: Polygon) => poly.map((q) => `${q.x.toFixed(3)},${q.y.toFixed(3)}`).join(" ");

/** Phase colours: lock steel, unlock ochre, impulse ruby, drop green. Shared with the page palette. */
const PHASE_COLOUR: Record<string, string> = {
  lock: "#2b5c8a", unlock: "#b07d10", impulse: "#b2322b", drop: "#4e7d3a",
};
const PHASE_NAME: Record<string, string> = { lock: "Lock", unlock: "Unlock", impulse: "Impulse", drop: "Drop" };

const INK = "#1c2733";

/** Drafting centre mark: a small cross through a pivot. Pure decoration around a point the sim supplied. */
const centreMark = (c: Vec, r: number) =>
  `<g class="centremark"><line x1="${c.x - r}" y1="${c.y}" x2="${c.x + r}" y2="${c.y}"/><line x1="${c.x}" y1="${c.y - r}" x2="${c.x}" y2="${c.y + r}"/></g>`;

export function renderMovement(p: EscapementParams, s: EscapementPose, timeMs?: number): string {
  const g = shapes(p, s);
  const R = p.wheelRadius;
  const top = g.balanceCentre.y + g.balanceRadius + 24;
  const bottom = -R - 24;
  const half = Math.max(R, g.balanceRadius) + 44;
  const colour = PHASE_COLOUR[s.phase];
  const stone = (st: Stone, name: string) => {
    const active = s.contact?.stone === name;
    return `<polygon class="stone ${active ? "active" : ""}" points="${pts(stoneOutline(st))}"/>` +
      `<line class="face" x1="${st.corner.x}" y1="${st.corner.y}" x2="${st.letoff.x}" y2="${st.letoff.y}"/>`;
  };
  const bankings = g.bankings.map((q) => `<circle class="banking" cx="${q.x}" cy="${q.y}" r="1.8"/>`).join("");
  const spokes = [0, 60, 120].map((a) => {
    const ang = (a + s.balanceAngle) * Math.PI / 180;
    const q1 = add(g.balanceCentre, polar(g.balanceRadius, ang)), q2 = add(g.balanceCentre, polar(g.balanceRadius, ang + Math.PI));
    return `<line class="spoke" x1="${q1.x}" y1="${q1.y}" x2="${q2.x}" y2="${q2.y}"/>`;
  }).join("");
  const contactDot = (() => {
    if (!s.contact) return "";
    // The tooth tip nearest the active stone's faces.
    const st = s.contact.stone === "entry" ? g.entryStone : g.exitStone;
    let best: Vec | null = null, bd = Infinity;
    for (const tooth of g.teeth) {
      const tip = tooth[0];
      const dd = Math.min(Math.hypot(tip.x - st.corner.x, tip.y - st.corner.y), Math.hypot(tip.x - st.letoff.x, tip.y - st.letoff.y));
      if (dd < bd) { bd = dd; best = tip; }
    }
    return best ? `<circle class="contact" cx="${best.x}" cy="${best.y}" r="2.6"/>` : "";
  })();
  const note = s.contact ? `${PHASE_NAME[s.phase]} on the ${s.contact.stone} pallet, ${s.contact.face} face` : `${PHASE_NAME[s.phase]}, wheel free`;

  return `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${-half} ${-top} ${2 * half} ${top - bottom}" data-phase="${s.phase}" font-family="Avenir Next, Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
  <style>
    .wheel { fill: #fbfcf8; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 1 }
    .tooth { fill: #fbfcf8; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.9; stroke-linejoin: round }
    .stone { fill: #e4e9ee; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.9 }
    .stone.active { fill: ${colour}2e }
    .face { stroke: ${colour}; stroke-width: 1.6; stroke-linecap: round }
    .lever { fill: #fbfcf8; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 1 }
    .pivot { fill: #fbfcf8; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.9 }
    .centremark line { stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.5 }
    .balance { fill: none; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 3.2 }
    .balance-inner { fill: none; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.5 }
    .spoke { stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.7 }
    .pin { fill: #b2322b; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.5 }
    .centreline { fill: none; stroke: #7c8792; stroke-width: 0.5; stroke-dasharray: 6 2 1.2 2 }
    .banking { fill: ${INK} }
    .contact { fill: none; stroke: ${colour}; stroke-width: 1.1 }
    .label { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #4a5663 }
    .phase { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; fill: ${colour} }
    .swatch { fill: ${colour} }
  </style>
  <g transform="scale(1,-1)">
    <circle class="centreline" cx="0" cy="0" r="${R}"/>
    <circle class="wheel" cx="0" cy="0" r="${0.8 * R}"/>
    ${g.teeth.map((t) => `<polygon class="tooth" points="${pts(t)}"/>`).join("")}
    ${centreMark({ x: 0, y: 0 }, 0.9 * R)}
    <circle class="pivot" cx="0" cy="0" r="2.2"/>
    ${g.arms.map((a) => `<polygon class="lever" points="${pts(a)}"/>`).join("")}
    <polygon class="lever" points="${pts(g.lever)}"/>
    ${stone(g.entryStone, "entry")}
    ${stone(g.exitStone, "exit")}
    <circle class="pivot" cx="${g.forkPivot.x}" cy="${g.forkPivot.y}" r="2.2"/>
    ${bankings}
    <circle class="centreline" cx="${g.balanceCentre.x}" cy="${g.balanceCentre.y}" r="${g.pinRadius}"/>
    ${centreMark(g.balanceCentre, g.balanceRadius + 8)}
    <circle class="balance" cx="${g.balanceCentre.x}" cy="${g.balanceCentre.y}" r="${g.balanceRadius}"/>
    ${spokes}
    <circle class="pivot" cx="${g.balanceCentre.x}" cy="${g.balanceCentre.y}" r="2.2"/>
    <circle class="pin" cx="${g.impulsePin.x}" cy="${g.impulsePin.y}" r="2.6"/>
    ${contactDot}
  </g>
  <rect class="swatch" x="${-half + 6}" y="${-top + 7}" width="4" height="10"/>
  <text class="phase" x="${-half + 15}" y="${-top + 16}">${note}</text>
  <text class="label" x="${-half + 15}" y="${-top + 29}">balance ${s.balanceAngle.toFixed(1)}°, fork ${s.forkAngle.toFixed(2)}°, wheel ${s.wheelAngle.toFixed(2)}°${timeMs === undefined ? "" : `, t = ${timeMs.toFixed(1)} ms`}</text>
</svg>`;
}

/** Timegrapher panel: trace plus readouts. Reads a Reading; computes nothing but pixels. */
import type { Reading } from "../core/timegrapher/analyze";

export interface TimegrapherView {
  reading: Reading | null;
  nominalPeriod: number;
  liftAngle: number;
  running: boolean;
  knocking: boolean;
  /** Sim seconds the trace spans, for the honest label. */
  spanSeconds: number;
  /** Sim seconds per wall second, for the honest label. */
  speedup: number;
}

const fmt = (x: number, d: number) => (Math.abs(x) < 0.5 * 10 ** -d ? "" : x > 0 ? "+" : "−") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(d);

export function renderTimegrapher(v: TimegrapherView): string {
  const W = 420, H = 300, pad = 36;
  const beatMs = (v.nominalPeriod / 2) * 1000;
  const yRange = Math.min(20, beatMs / 2); // ±20 ms, wrapping like a real machine's screen
  const r = v.reading;
  const dots = r
    ? r.trace.map((p) => {
        const x = pad + ((W - 2 * pad) * p.beat) / Math.max(1, r.trace.length - 1);
        let off = ((p.offsetMs + yRange) % (2 * yRange) + 2 * yRange) % (2 * yRange) - yRange; // wrap
        const y = H / 2 - (off / yRange) * (H / 2 - pad);
        return `<circle class="dot p${p.parity}" cx="${x.toFixed(1)}" cy="${y.toFixed(1)}" r="1.5"/>`;
      }).join("")
    : "";
  const rate = r && v.running ? fmt(r.rateSecondsPerDay, 0) : "—";
  const amp = r && v.running ? r.amplitudeDeg.toFixed(0) : "—";
  const be = r && v.running ? r.beatErrorMs.toFixed(1) : "—";
  // Faint horizontal grid at ±10 ms: half the screen range, purely a reading aid.
  const gridY = [H / 2 - (H / 2 - pad) / 2, H / 2 + (H / 2 - pad) / 2];
  return `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H + 84}" class="timegrapher" data-rate="${r?.rateSecondsPerDay ?? ""}">
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="${W}" height="${H}" rx="2" class="screen"/>
  <rect x="0.5" y="0.5" width="${W - 1}" height="${H - 1}" rx="2" class="screen-edge"/>
  ${gridY.map((y) => `<line x1="${pad}" y1="${y}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${y}" class="grid"/>`).join("")}
  <line x1="${pad}" y1="${H / 2}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${H / 2}" class="axis"/>
  <text x="${pad}" y="${pad - 10}" class="axislabel">+${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
  <text x="${pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel">−${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
  <text x="${W - pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel" text-anchor="end">${v.spanSeconds.toFixed(0)} s of ticks at ${v.speedup}× time</text>
  ${v.knocking ? `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">Knocking: amplitude unreliable</text>` : ""}
  ${v.running ? dots : `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">No signal. The watch has stopped.</text>`}
  <g class="readouts" transform="translate(0,${H + 10})">
    <line x1="${W / 3}" y1="8" x2="${W / 3}" y2="56" class="divider"/>
    <line x1="${2 * W / 3}" y1="8" x2="${2 * W / 3}" y2="56" class="divider"/>
    <text x="${pad}" y="34" class="big">${rate}<tspan class="unit"> s/day</tspan></text>
    <text x="${W / 2}" y="34" class="big" text-anchor="middle">${amp}<tspan class="unit">°</tspan></text>
    <text x="${W - pad}" y="34" class="big" text-anchor="end">${be}<tspan class="unit"> ms</tspan></text>
    <text x="${pad}" y="56" class="small">rate</text>
    <text x="${W / 2}" y="56" class="small" text-anchor="middle">amplitude at ${v.liftAngle}° lift angle</text>
    <text x="${W - pad}" y="56" class="small" text-anchor="end">beat error</text>
  </g>
</svg>`;
}

import { VINTAGE_18000 } from "./catalog/vintage18000";
import { readWatch, ZERO_SETTINGS, POSITIONS, type WatchSettings, type WatchReading, type WatchSpec } from "./core/watch";
import { nominalPeriod } from "./core/oscillator/period";
import { initialPose, step, type EscapementPose, type Phase } from "./core/escapement/kinematics";
import { shapes, stonePenetration } from "./core/escapement/shapes";
import { derived } from "./core/escapement/params";
import { CONTACT_TOL } from "./core/escapement/kinematics";
import { analyze, type Reading } from "./core/timegrapher/analyze";
import { advanceTicks, emptyWindow, type TickWindow } from "./app/ticker";
import { renderMovement } from "./view/movement";
import { renderTimegrapher } from "./view/timegrapher";
import { PUZZLES, type Puzzle } from "./puzzles";
import { STATES } from "./verify/states";

const calibre = VINTAGE_18000;
const esc = calibre.escapement;
const T = nominalPeriod(calibre.beatRate);
const TRACE_BEATS = 300;
/** Timegrapher clock runs this many times faster than the wall clock (decision: two clocks). */
const SIM_SPEEDUP = 10;

// ---------- state ----------
let puzzle: Puzzle | null = PUZZLES[0];
let user: WatchSettings = { ...ZERO_SETTINGS };
let animSpeed = 1;
let animPaused = false;
let animTime = T / 4;
let simTime = 0;
let win: TickWindow = emptyWindow();
let pose: EscapementPose = initialPose(esc, 0);
let reading: WatchReading = readWatch(calibre.watch, user);
let tg: Reading | null = null;
let heldSeconds = 0;
let solved = false;
let answered: number | null = null;
let lastWall = performance.now();

const spec = (): WatchSpec => (puzzle?.specOverride ? puzzle.specOverride(calibre.watch) : calibre.watch);
const effective = (): WatchSettings => {
  const f = puzzle?.faults ?? {};
  return {
    ...user,
    regulatorIndex: user.regulatorIndex + (f.regulatorIndex ?? 0),
    beatOffsetDeg: user.beatOffsetDeg + (f.beatOffsetDeg ?? 0),
    unbalance: user.unbalance + (f.unbalance ?? 0),
    heavySpotDeg: f.heavySpotDeg ?? user.heavySpotDeg,
    inertiaTrim: user.inertiaTrim,
  };
};

// ---------- DOM ----------
const $ = <T extends HTMLElement>(id: string) => document.getElementById(id) as T;
const movementEl = $("movement"), tgEl = $("timegrapher"), puzzleEl = $("puzzle");

function balanceAngleAt(t: number) {
  return reading.running ? reading.amplitudeDeg * Math.sin((2 * Math.PI * t) / reading.period) - reading.beatOffsetDeg : -reading.beatOffsetDeg;
}

function recompute() {
  reading = readWatch(spec(), effective());
}

function drawMovement() {
  movementEl.innerHTML = renderMovement(esc, pose, animTime * 1000);
  if (!reading.running) movementEl.querySelector(".phase")!.textContent = "STOPPED · no torque at the escape wheel";
}
function drawTimegrapher() {
  tgEl.innerHTML = renderTimegrapher({ reading: tg, nominalPeriod: T, liftAngle: calibre.liftAngle, running: reading.running, knocking: reading.knocking, spanSeconds: (TRACE_BEATS * T) / 2, speedup: SIM_SPEEDUP });
}
function drawPuzzle() {
  if (!puzzle) { puzzleEl.innerHTML = `<h2>Free play</h2><p>Adjust anything. The timegrapher shows what a watchmaker would see.</p>`; return; }
  const idx = PUZZLES.indexOf(puzzle);
  puzzleEl.innerHTML = `<h2>Puzzle ${idx + 1} · ${puzzle.title}</h2>
    <p class="symptom">${puzzle.symptom}</p>
    <p class="goal"><strong>Goal:</strong> ${puzzle.goal}</p>
    ${Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds) ? `<div class="hold"><div class="bar" style="width:${Math.min(100, (100 * heldSeconds) / puzzle.holdSeconds).toFixed(1)}%"></div><span>${solved ? "solved" : `${heldSeconds.toFixed(0)} / ${puzzle.holdSeconds} s in band`}</span></div>` : ""}
    ${puzzle.question ? `<div class="question"><p>${puzzle.question.prompt}</p>${puzzle.question.choices.map((c, i) => `<button class="choice ${answered === i ? (i === puzzle!.question!.correct ? "right" : "wrong") : ""}" data-choice="${i}">${c}</button>`).join("")}${answered !== null ? `<p class="verdict">${answered === puzzle.question.correct ? puzzle.question.whyCorrect : "Not quite. Watch the rate as the wind runs down, then try again."}</p>` : ""}</div>` : ""}
    ${solved ? `<details open><summary>Why it worked</summary><p>${puzzle.explanation}</p></details>` : ""}`;
  puzzleEl.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>(".choice").forEach((b) => (b.onclick = () => { answered = Number(b.dataset.choice); if (answered === puzzle!.question!.correct) solved = true; drawPuzzle(); }));
}
function drawControls() {
  const show = (name: string) => !puzzle || puzzle.controls.includes(name as never) || puzzle.controls.length === 0;
  for (const name of ["regulator", "beat", "wind", "screws", "position"]) $(`ctl-${name}`).hidden = !show(name);
  $("ctl-poise").hidden = $("ctl-poise-angle").hidden = !show("poise");
  $("readout-rate").textContent = reading.running ? `${reading.rateSecondsPerDay >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(reading.rateSecondsPerDay).toFixed(1)} s/day true rate` : "stopped";
}

// ---------- frame loop ----------
function frame(now: number) {
  const wallDt = Math.min(0.1, (now - lastWall) / 1000);
  lastWall = now;
  if (!animPaused) {
    const dt = wallDt * animSpeed;
    animTime += dt;
    pose = step(esc, pose, balanceAngleAt(animTime), Math.max(dt, 1e-6));
    drawMovement();
  }
  // Timegrapher clock.
  const simDt = wallDt * SIM_SPEEDUP;
  simTime += simDt;
  win = advanceTicks(win, reading, simTime, TRACE_BEATS);
  tg = analyze(win.ticks, T, calibre.liftAngle);
  drawTimegrapher();
  if (puzzle && !solved && Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds)) {
    heldSeconds = puzzle.band(reading, tg) ? heldSeconds + simDt : 0;
    if (heldSeconds >= puzzle.holdSeconds) solved = true;
    drawPuzzle();
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}

// ---------- controls ----------
// Poising control: built here (not in index.html) because it arrived after the layout was handed to design.
{
  const footer = document.querySelector("footer")!;
  const anchor = $("ctl-position");

    const l = document.createElement("label"); l.id = `ctl-${id}`;
    l.innerHTML = `${label} <input id="${id}" type="range" min="${min}" max="${max}" step="${step}" value="0" /><span class="value" id="${id}-value"></span>`;
    footer.insertBefore(l, anchor);
  };
  mk("poise", "Poising: remove weight (µg·cm)", 0, 15, 0.25);
  mk("poise-angle", "Poising: at rim position (°)", 0, 360, 5);
  const wrap = document.createElement("div"); wrap.id = "ctl-poise-group"; // keep hide/show simple
  footer.insertBefore(wrap, anchor);
  wrap.append($("ctl-poise"), $("ctl-poise-angle"));
  wrap.style.display = "contents";
}
function bindRange(id: string, key: keyof WatchSettings, fmt: (v: number) => string) {
  const el = $<HTMLInputElement>(id), out = $(`${id}-value`);
  const apply = () => { (user as any)[key] = Number(el.value); out.textContent = fmt(Number(el.value)); recompute(); drawControls(); };
  el.oninput = apply; apply();
}
bindRange("regulator", "regulatorIndex", (v) => `${v >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(v).toFixed(2)}° ${v > 0 ? "(toward F)" : v < 0 ? "(toward S)" : ""}`);
bindRange("beat", "beatOffsetDeg", (v) => `${v.toFixed(1)}°`);
bindRange("wind", "hoursSinceWind", (v) => `${v.toFixed(0)} h since wound`);
bindRange("screws", "inertiaTrim", (v) => `${(v * 100).toFixed(2)} % inertia`);
{
  const amt = $<HTMLInputElement>("poise"), ang = $<HTMLInputElement>("poise-angle");
  const apply = () => {
    user.poiseCorrection = Number(amt.value) * 1e-11; user.poiseCorrectionDeg = Number(ang.value);
    $("poise-value").textContent = `${Number(amt.value).toFixed(2)} µg·cm`; $("poise-angle-value").textContent = `${ang.value}° on the rim`;
    recompute(); drawControls();
  };
  amt.oninput = apply; ang.oninput = apply; apply();
}
$<HTMLSelectElement>("position").onchange = (e) => { user.position = (e.target as HTMLSelectElement).value as WatchSettings["position"]; recompute(); drawControls(); };
$<HTMLSelectElement>("position").innerHTML = POSITIONS.map((p) => `<option value="${p.id}">${p.label}</option>`).join("");
$<HTMLSelectElement>("speed").onchange = (e) => { animSpeed = Number((e.target as HTMLSelectElement).value); };
$("pause").onclick = () => { animPaused = !animPaused; $("pause").textContent = animPaused ? "Play" : "Pause"; };

function timeForPhase(phase: Phase, beat: 0 | 1, frac: number): number {
  // Scan one period from T/4 with a fresh pose, find the phase window on the requested beat.
  const N = 4000;
  let p = initialPose(esc, balanceAngleAt(T / 4));
  let t = T / 4, start: number | null = null, found: [number, number] | null = null, beatIdx = -1, lastPhase: Phase = p.phase;
  for (let i = 1; i <= N && !found; i++) {
    const nt = T / 4 + (i / N) * T;
    p = step(esc, p, balanceAngleAt(nt), nt - t); t = nt;
    if (p.phase === "unlock" && lastPhase === "lock") beatIdx++;
    if (beatIdx === beat && p.phase === phase && start === null) start = t;
    if (start !== null && p.phase !== phase) found = [start, t];
    lastPhase = p.phase;
  }
  return found ? found[0] + frac * (found[1] - found[0]) : T / 4;
}

    out.push({ name: "lever within bankings", pass: Math.abs(pose.forkAngle) <= derived(esc).forkHalf + 1e-9, detail: `fork ${pose.forkAngle.toFixed(3)}°` });

/** Named states for the verify-render skill. Each sets puzzle, settings and animation phase. */
import type { WatchSettings } from "../core/watch";
import type { Phase } from "../core/escapement/kinematics";

export interface NamedState {
  describe: string;
  puzzle: string | null;
  settings: Partial<WatchSettings>;
  /** Freeze the animation at the middle of this escapement phase on this beat (0 entry, 1 exit). */

  /** Simulated seconds of ticks to accumulate before the shot. */
  simSeconds: number;
  expect: { phase?: Phase; rateWithin?: [number, number]; amplitudeWithin?: [number, number]; beatErrorBelow?: number; running?: boolean };
}

export const STATES: Record<string, NamedState> = {

  // Heavy spot at the bottom when crown up; at 250° (above the 219.5° crossover) that is a LOSS. See docs/research/04.
  "position-crown-up": { describe: "Puzzle 4 crown up: amplitude ~250°, heavy spot at the bottom, poise error showing as a loss of several s/day.", puzzle: "position-error", settings: { position: "CU" }, simSeconds: 120, expect: { amplitudeWithin: [245, 255], rateWithin: [-15, -2], running: true } },

-----SKILL
---
name: verify-render
description: Verify that the movement renders correctly. Use after any change to shapes, the renderer, the sim core, or a named state, before saying a visual is done, and when a user reports a render that looks wrong. Screenshots named states via Playwright and runs numeric geometry checks the page exposes.
---

# verify-render

Vision alone misses fine geometry. This skill pairs screenshots with numbers: the page exposes
named states and a `check()` that returns pass/fail assertions computed from the same shapes
the renderer draws. The script drives both and reports like a test run.

## Contract the app must honour

- `?state=<name>` in the URL loads a named state, paused.
- `window.__bench` exists after render with:
  - `states(): string[]` — every named state.
  - `check(): { name: string; pass: boolean; detail: string }[]` — numeric assertions for the
    state currently shown (no overlap, contact on the expected face, lever within bankings,
    anything the state declares it expects).
  - `describe(): string` — one line: what this state is supposed to show.
- The root `<svg>` carries `data-state="<name>"` once rendered.

Named states and their expectations live in `src/verify/states.ts` (root app) or
`spike/src/states.ts` (spike). A new visual feature adds a state there; it never adds a check
to the renderer.

## Steps

1. Run the script from the app directory. It starts the Vite dev server itself.
   ```
   node .claude/skills/verify-render/scripts/verify-render.mjs --root <app dir> [--state <name>]
   ```
   It writes `shots/<state>.png` under the app dir and prints one line per check. Exit code is
   non-zero if any check fails or any state fails to render.
2. **Read every screenshot** with the Read tool. For each, compare the frame against the
   state's `describe()` line printed above it. Decide: does the picture show what the line
   says? Numbers catch overlap; only eyes catch "the stone is on the wrong side of the wheel".
3. Report in three groups: numeric failures (quote the detail line), visual disagreements
   (name the frame and what is off), and frames that pass both. A state passes only when both
   agree.
4. Fix in the sim or shapes, never by editing a check's tolerance or a state's expectation to
   match the picture. If an expectation was genuinely wrong, say so in the transcript and
   change it in `states.ts` with a one-line comment giving the reason.

Done when every state passes both the numbers and your eyes, or the remaining failures are
listed with a cause for each.

/** SVG renderer. Reads state, computes nothing: every coordinate comes from shapes(). */
import { type EscapementParams } from "../core/escapement/params";
import { type EscapementPose } from "../core/escapement/kinematics";
import { shapes, stoneOutline, type Stone } from "../core/escapement/shapes";
import { type Polygon, type Vec, polar, add } from "../core/escapement/geom2d";

const pts = (poly: Polygon) => poly.map((q) => `${q.x.toFixed(3)},${q.y.toFixed(3)}`).join(" ");
const rad = (deg: number) => (deg * Math.PI) / 180;

/** Phase colours: lock steel, unlock ochre, impulse ruby, drop green. Shared with the page palette. */
const PHASE_COLOUR: Record<string, string> = {
  lock: "#2b5c8a", unlock: "#b07d10", impulse: "#b2322b", drop: "#4e7d3a",
};
const PHASE_NAME: Record<string, string> = { lock: "Lock", unlock: "Unlock", impulse: "Impulse", drop: "Drop" };

/* Drawing palette: blue-black ink on paper, brass for the wheel and lever, ruby for every jewel. */
const INK = "#1c2733";
const INK_FAINT = "#8d97a0";
const PAPER = "#fbfcf8";
const BRASS = "#f1ead6";
const RUBY = "#b2322b";
const RUBY_PALE = "#f2d9d6";

/** Drafting centre mark: a small cross through a pivot. Pure decoration around a point the sim supplied. */
const centreMark = (c: Vec, r: number) =>
  `<g class="centremark"><line x1="${c.x - r}" y1="${c.y}" x2="${c.x + r}" y2="${c.y}"/><line x1="${c.x}" y1="${c.y - r}" x2="${c.x}" y2="${c.y + r}"/></g>`;

/** A jewelled pivot: ruby hole jewel with the pivot drawn through it. */
const pivot = (c: Vec) =>
  `<circle class="jewel" cx="${c.x}" cy="${c.y}" r="3.4"/><circle class="pivot" cx="${c.x}" cy="${c.y}" r="1.3"/>`;

export function renderMovement(p: EscapementParams, s: EscapementPose, timeMs?: number): string {
  const g = shapes(p, s);
  const R = p.wheelRadius;
  // Margins: room above the balance for the two-line caption, a little either side.
  const top = g.balanceCentre.y + g.balanceRadius + 46;
  const bottom = -R - 22;
  const half = Math.max(R, g.balanceRadius) + 40;
  const colour = PHASE_COLOUR[s.phase];
  const stone = (st: Stone, name: string) => {
    const active = s.contact?.stone === name;
    return `<polygon class="stone ${active ? "active" : ""}" points="${pts(stoneOutline(st))}"/>` +
      `<line class="face" x1="${st.corner.x}" y1="${st.corner.y}" x2="${st.letoff.x}" y2="${st.letoff.y}"/>`;
  };
  const bankings = g.bankings.map((q) => `<circle class="banking" cx="${q.x}" cy="${q.y}" r="2"/>`).join("");
  // Balance: three crossing arms through the centre, turning with the balance.
  const spokes = [0, 60, 120].map((a) => {
    const ang = rad(a + s.balanceAngle);
    const q1 = add(g.balanceCentre, polar(g.balanceRadius, ang)), q2 = add(g.balanceCentre, polar(g.balanceRadius, ang + Math.PI));
    return `<line class="spoke" x1="${q1.x}" y1="${q1.y}" x2="${q2.x}" y2="${q2.y}"/>`;
  }).join("");
  // Escape wheel: a crossed-out brass wheel, five arms turning with the teeth (same angle convention as toothPolygons).
  const arms = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4].map((k) => {
    const ang = rad(90 - s.wheelAngle + k * 72);
    const q1 = polar(0.14 * R, ang), q2 = polar(0.66 * R, ang);

  }).join("");

    if (!s.contact) return "";
    // The tooth tip nearest the active stone's faces.
    const st = s.contact.stone === "entry" ? g.entryStone : g.exitStone;
    let best: Vec | null = null, bd = Infinity;
    for (const tooth of g.teeth) {

      if (dd < bd) { bd = dd; best = tip; }
    }
    return best ? `<circle class="contact" cx="${best.x}" cy="${best.y}" r="3.2"/>` : "";
  })();
  const note = s.contact ? `${PHASE_NAME[s.phase]} on the ${s.contact.stone} pallet, ${s.contact.face} face` : `${PHASE_NAME[s.phase]}, wheel free`;

    .stone { fill: ${RUBY_PALE}; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.9 }
    .stone.active { fill: ${colour}33 }
    .face { stroke: ${colour}; stroke-width: 1.8; stroke-linecap: round }
    .lever { fill: ${BRASS}; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 1 }
    .jewel { fill: ${RUBY_PALE}; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.7 }
    .pivot { fill: ${INK} }
    .centremark line { stroke: ${INK_FAINT}; stroke-width: 0.5 }
    .balance { fill: none; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 3.4 }
    .spoke { stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.8 }
    .pin { fill: ${RUBY}; stroke: ${INK}; stroke-width: 0.5 }
    .centreline { fill: none; stroke: ${INK_FAINT}; stroke-width: 0.5; stroke-dasharray: 6 2 1.2 2 }
    .banking { fill: ${INK} }
    .contact { fill: none; stroke: ${colour}; stroke-width: 1.2 }
    .label { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #4a5663 }
    .phase { font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 600; fill: ${colour} }
    .swatch { fill: ${colour} }
  </style>
  <g transform="scale(1,-1)">
    <circle class="centreline" cx="0" cy="0" r="${R}"/>
    <circle class="wheel" cx="0" cy="0" r="${0.8 * R}"/>
    <circle class="wheel-web" cx="0" cy="0" r="${0.68 * R}"/>

    ${pivot(g.forkPivot)}
    ${bankings}

    <circle class="balance" cx="${g.balanceCentre.x}" cy="${g.balanceCentre.y}" r="${g.balanceRadius}"/>
    ${spokes}
    ${pivot(g.balanceCentre)}
    <circle class="pin" cx="${g.impulsePin.x}" cy="${g.impulsePin.y}" r="2.6"/>
    ${contactDot}
  </g>
  <rect class="swatch" x="${-half + 4}" y="${-top + 6}" width="4" height="11"/>
  <text class="phase" x="${-half + 13}" y="${-top + 16}">${note}</text>
  <text class="label" x="${-half + 13}" y="${-top + 29}">balance ${s.balanceAngle.toFixed(1)}°, fork ${s.forkAngle.toFixed(2)}°, wheel ${s.wheelAngle.toFixed(2)}°${timeMs === undefined ? "" : `, t = ${timeMs.toFixed(1)} ms`}</text>
</svg>`;
}
